calibration.rollingRecord: Settled-close gates 6 for 8 this week; the discretionary overlay on top of them 1 for 6.
calibration.note: The endday REDUCE gate at 80,750.0 did NOT fire. The six hourly closes since read 80,970.1, 80,803.4, 80,838.5, 81,070.0, 80,990.5 and 80,808.5 - the lowest is 58.5 points ABOVE the trigger, so the settled-close discipline held even though the intrabar low reached 80,571.8. The endday ADD gate at 82,300.0 was never approached; the overnight high is 81,433.9, 866.1 points short. actingHelped is TRUE for the first time in six sessions: the endday session trimmed 10 percent of the spot core at 81,283.9 and spot now marks 80,923.6, so that slice was sold 360.3 points HIGHER than the current mark. The uncomfortable detail sits between those two facts. The endday session also switched ON a resting stop at 80,700, and price traded to 80,571.8 at 06:15-06:30 UTC before closing the hour back at 80,808.5. Had that stop been a live order rather than guidance it would have filled 223.6 points below the current mark, turning a correct call into a losing execution. The settled-close gate was right and the resting stop placed inside the same noise band was wrong, on the same night, on the same level. The lesson is that a stop and a settled-close trigger are different instruments and must not be placed at the same price: tonight's gate sits at 80,550 and the stop 100 points lower again at 80,450, both outside the wick that just happened.
